wire.headline: Thornwater Group Faces Backlash Over Tariff Hike Amidst Debt Concerns
sentences: Thornwater Group has confirmed a 12% tariff increase that will take effect on April 1.
CEO Marian Holt cited aging pipes as the primary driver for the proposed price hikes.
The company reported that 4,800 leaks were repaired during the previous fiscal year.
As a result of the changes, the average household bill is set to rise to 12.4p per day by July.
Regulator Ofgem has approved a 310m GBP investment plan for infrastructure improvements.
According to recent filings, the company's total debt stands at 4.26bn GBP.
Shares fell by 4.5% in early trading on the London Stock Exchange following the announcement.
An investor call is scheduled for 4 November to discuss the company's outlook.
